root_cause.text: The vulnerability is caused by incorrect end-of-list detection in `cgroup_storage_get_next_key()`, where a NULL check following `list_next_entry()` is ineffective because the macro wraps to the list head instead of returning NULL, resulting in reading aliased internal map memory.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "`list_next_entry()` never returns NULL -- when the current element is the last entry it wraps to the list head via container_of()" and the patch replaces the dead code `if (!storage)` with `if (list_entry_is_head(storage, &map->list, list_map))` in `kernel/bpf/local_storage.c`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix list iteration termination detection by using list_entry_is_head() instead of NULL check to prevent premature exit or infinite loop during cgroup storage map traversal
intent_record.what: Changed line 273 from 'if (!storage)' to 'if (list_entry_is_head(storage, &map->list, list_map))' to properly detect end of list iteration
intent_record.how: Replaces a NULL pointer check with a proper list traversal termination check using list_entry_is_head(), which correctly identifies when iteration has reached the list head in a circular doubly-linked list structure

grouping_result.intent: Fix list iteration termination detection by using list_entry_is_head() instead of NULL check to prevent premature exit or infinite loop during cgroup storage map traversal

relevance_review.reason: The group's core intent directly addresses the vulnerability root cause. The root cause identifies incorrect end-of-list detection using a NULL check after list_next_entry(), and the proposed fix replaces this with list_entry_is_head(), which correctly handles the circular nature of kernel linked lists.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement calls list_next_entry() which wraps to the list head when reaching the end of the list instead of returning NULL. The subsequent NULL check or list_entry_is_head() check becomes ineffective because the macro never returns NULL, allowing iteration to continue past the valid entries and read aliased internal map memory.
